analyzed_vuln.description: `hb_vector_t::alloc()` grows an inline-backed vector by raw `memcpy` of `Type` objects from `static_array` into heap storage (line 166) but leaves the original inline objects intact. For non-trivially-owning elements such as `cff1_font_dict_values_t` (which contains a nested `hb_vector_t<op_str_t>`), this duplicates ownership pointers. CFF cleanup frees the nested vector through the heap copy; later the outer vector's implicit destruction also destroys its original `static_array` elements and frees the same nested allocation, causing the observed double-free. The second free occurs in `hb_vector_t<op_str_t>::fini()` during destruction of `fontDicts`' stale inline element.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A supplied OpenType face must contain a CID-keyed CFF1 table whose FDArray causes `fontDicts` to exceed its 8-element inline capacity, so `hb_vector_t<cff1_font_dict_values_t>::alloc()` relocates the first elements with `memcpy`. At least one relocated early Font DICT must record enough operators to make its nested `values` vector heap-backed (more than its 8 inline entries). The PoC's large FDArray satisfies this; a later CFF parsing/sanitization failure makes `accelerator_templ_t::init()` call `fini()`, which frees the heap copy, and scope exit/destruction frees the stale inline alias. The font bytes flow from the fuzzer into `hb_face_t`, then `hb_subset()` -> `_populate_gids_to_retain()` -> CFF accelerator initialization.

args: In harfbuzz/src/hb-vector.hh, analyze hb_vector_t::alloc() when transitioning from static_array to heap storage. Given that it byte-copies Type elements and static_array elements are later implicitly destructed, what relocation/ownership convention does this old HarfBuzz codebase use, and is clearing the source static_array after memcpy the compatible root fix? Please identify any nearby lifecycle assumptions or analogous transfer patterns in the C++ source.

The sanitizer report shows a double-free for hb_vector_t<CFF::cff1_font_dict_values_t,8>, whose early inline element contains a heap-backed nested hb_vector_t<CFF::op_str_t,8>. At alloc line 166 the outer vector memcpy-copies inline elements into calloc'd heap storage, leaving the source nested vector pointer alive. CFF fini_deep frees the heap copy's nested allocation, then the outer vector object's static_array member destructors run and the stale source alias frees it again. The existing vector uses calloc/realloc and raw memset rather than placement-new or conventional C++ move construction, and fini() only frees arrayZ_, so I suspect its intended convention is bitwise relocation and that the source bytes must be zeroed after a successful inline-to-heap copy. I want confirmation against project idioms before patching harfbuzz/src/hb-vector.hh.
